quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #20
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Oncoming traffic and pedestrians must yield to you.
Never yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: When turning left, you must let oncoming traffic and pedestrians pass first. You can only turn when it is safe and the traffic signal allows it.

questions.question: You see a flashing red light at an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Come to a full stop and go when it is safe.
Stop only if other cars are also approaching.
Stop only if other cars are already in the intersection.
Slow down and stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a full stop and go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must stop completely, check the intersection, and only go when it is safe.

questions.question: The posted speed limit is the fastest you can drive in an area.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: The posted speed limit is the fastest legal speed under good conditions. You must drive slower when conditions are bad, like wet roads or poor visibility.

questions.question: What helps drivers save gasoline?

options.text: Letting the car run in the driveway.
Speeding up quickly.
Slowing down gradually.
Stopping suddenly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowing down gradually.
questions.explanation: Every sudden stop uses fuel to speed back up. If you look ahead and slow down gradually or change lanes to avoid braking, you use less gas.

questions.question: How can you prevent hydroplaning?

options.text: Make sure your tires have good tread.
Keep your tires inflated to the right pressure.
Drive slower in the rain.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: To prevent hydroplaning, keep your tires in good condition with proper tread and pressure. Also drive slower when it rains, since hydroplaning happens more often at high speeds.

questions.question: On a road with no sidewalk, where should a pedestrian walk?

options.text: On the side with the least traffic.
On the same side traffic is moving.
On the side facing oncoming traffic.
On the side with the most traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the side facing oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians should walk facing the traffic coming toward them. This way they can see vehicles and avoid danger.

questions.question: When turning onto a street with multiple lanes in your direction, which lane should you enter?

options.text: The lane closest to the one you came from.
The lane marked with an arrow.
The middle lane.
Any lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to the one you came from.
questions.explanation: Turn into the lane nearest to your original lane. Do not change lanes while turning.

questions.question: Which statement about blind spots is correct?

options.text: One outside mirror eliminates all blind spots.
Large trucks have bigger blind spots than regular cars.
You can see blind spots by looking in the rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks have bigger blind spots than regular cars.
questions.explanation: All vehicles have blind spots that mirrors cannot show. Large trucks have much larger blind spots than passenger cars.

questions.question: When can you park or stop on a freeway shoulder?

options.text: If you turn on your emergency flashers.
If no part of your car is on the road.
If you need to check directions.
Only in an emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only in an emergency.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on a freeway shoulder except when there is an emergency.

questions.question: When must you yield to emergency vehicles?

options.text: Never.
When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.
Only when other vehicles yield first.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.
questions.explanation: You must give emergency vehicles the right-of-way whenever you see flashing lights or hear a siren.

questions.question: When backing up, you should:

options.text: Use only your mirrors.
Flash your lights.
Open your door to check if it is safe.
Turn your head and look out the rear window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look out the rear window.
questions.explanation: Always check behind your vehicle before backing up. Children and small objects are hard to see from the driver's seat. Turn your head so you can see through the rear window. Do not rely only on mirrors or sensors.

questions.question: When pulling out of a driveway onto a street, you must:

options.text: Drive slowly so approaching vehicles and pedestrians can move out of your way.
Honk your horn so approaching vehicles and pedestrians know to give you space.
Stop and make sure no pedestrians or vehicles are coming.
You can ignore pedestrians if there is no sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and make sure no pedestrians or vehicles are coming.
questions.explanation: Always stop before entering the roadway from a driveway. Yield to any approaching vehicles or pedestrians crossing. Stop before crossing the sidewalk area. Failing to stop is illegal.

questions.question: Alcohol causes:

options.text: Loss of focus.
Poor coordination.
Slower decision-making.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol harms your vision, judgment, focus, and coordination.

questions.question: At a stop sign, you should stop and:

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for cars following too closely.
Go when the car ahead of you goes.
Look right, then left, then right again.
Look left, then right, then left again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look left, then right, then left again.
questions.explanation: At a stop sign, look left first because vehicles from the left are closer to you. Then look right. Finally, look left again in case you missed a vehicle.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: You can travel in either direction in this lane.
Traffic moves in both directions on this road.
You are approaching a divided highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in both directions on this road.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that traffic moves in both directions on this road.

questions.question: This sign shows:

options.text: The distance from the road to a bridge or overpass.
The maximum legal height of a vehicle in this state.
The maximum width of a vehicle allowed on the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: The distance from the road to a bridge or overpass.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of low clearance. It shows the distance from the road to the bottom of a bridge or overpass (in this case, 12 feet, 6 inches).

questions.question: To stay out of a truck or bus driver's blind spot, you should:

options.text: Never pass them.
Do not drive beside them and do not follow too closely.
Flash your lights at them.
Honk your horn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive beside them and do not follow too closely.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles have large blind spots on the sides and rear. Do not drive beside them and do not follow too closely.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly is always safe.
Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
Speed does not affect safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
questions.explanation: Driving too slowly can be dangerous because it frustrates drivers behind you and causes them to make unsafe moves to pass. Drive with the flow of traffic within the legal speed limit.

questions.question: To avoid becoming an aggressive driver:

options.text: Stay calm and focus on driving.
Drive faster than the posted speed limit.
Follow the car in front of you closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and focus on driving.
questions.explanation: To avoid becoming an aggressive driver, stay focused on driving and do not take the actions of other drivers personally. Be realistic about travel time, drive within the speed limit, and forgive other drivers.

questions.question: Driving at night is more dangerous than driving during the day because:

options.text: You cannot see as far ahead.
The road is always more slippery at night.
Your reaction time is slower at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as far ahead.
questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as far ahead because of reduced visibility and glare from oncoming headlights. Always use headlights and drive carefully in the dark.

questions.question: You may pass another vehicle if the line dividing your lane is a ____ line.

options.text: Broken white
Double solid yellow
Solid yellow
Solid white

questions.correctAnswerText: Broken white
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes going the same direction. You can cross broken white lines to pass if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: A solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line means that vehicles:

options.text: Driving in both directions may pass.
Next to the broken line may pass.
Next to the solid line may pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Next to the broken line may pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic going in opposite directions. If you are next to a broken yellow line, you may pass other vehicles.

questions.question: Which statement about blind spots is true?

options.text: They are eliminated if you have one outside mirror on each side of the vehicle.
Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.
Blind spots can be checked by looking in your rearview mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Large trucks have larger blind spots than regular cars, and other drivers should avoid these areas.

questions.question: Vehicles stopped behind a school bus with red lights flashing must remain stopped until:

options.text: All students are off the bus.
The stop arm is retracted.
The stop arm is retracted and the bus resumes motion.

questions.correctAnswerText: The stop arm is retracted and the bus resumes motion.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has flashing red lights and its stop arm extended, you must stay stopped until the lights turn off, the stop arm goes in, and the bus starts moving again.

questions.question: Driving is a privilege, not a right.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: Driving is a privilege, not a right. Having a driver's license means you have a serious responsibility to keep yourself and others safe.

questions.question: This sign warns drivers that:

options.text: The right lane is ending and traffic should merge left.
The road curves ahead.
There are upcoming intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane is ending and traffic should merge left.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to conditions ahead. This sign warns that a lane is ending and you should merge left.

questions.question: Remove all snow, frost, and ice from:

options.text: Just the windshield.
All windows.
Just the windshield and passenger window.

questions.correctAnswerText: All windows.
questions.explanation: You must see clearly through all your windows before driving. Remove all snow, ice, and frost from all windows and mirrors.

questions.question: A driver entering public traffic from a driveway or private road:

options.text: Has the right-of-way.
Should yield to drivers already on the public road.
May force their way into traffic.
Can assume that other drivers will change lanes to make room.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should yield to drivers already on the public road.
questions.explanation: When entering traffic from a driveway or private road, you must yield to drivers already on the public road. Merge safely when it is clear to do so.

questions.question: You can help keep the driver behind you a safe distance away by:

options.text: Driving 10 mph faster than the car behind you.
Driving 10 mph slower than the car behind you.
Maintaining a steady speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Maintaining a steady speed.
questions.explanation: Help keep a safe distance behind you by driving at a steady speed. Also signal your turns, lane changes, and slowing down in advance.

questions.question: Unless otherwise posted, the speed limit in a residential area is:

options.text: 45 mph.
35 mph.
25 mph.
15 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: 25 mph.
questions.explanation: The maximum speed limit in a residential area is 25 miles per hour. Follow any posted speed limit signs if they show a different speed.
